# Code of Conduct

This project is intended to be a professional, technically rigorous, and welcoming open-source space.

## Expected behavior

Contributors, reviewers, maintainers, and users are expected to:

- communicate respectfully and focus criticism on technical ideas, evidence, and outcomes;
- provide reproducible details when reporting defects or disputed behavior;
- acknowledge uncertainty, limitations, and conflicting evidence explicitly;
- respect privacy, credentials, access controls, and unpublished security information;
- avoid harassment, discriminatory language, personal attacks, threats, and sustained disruption;
- give appropriate credit for external data, software, documentation, and prior work.

## Unacceptable behavior

Unacceptable behavior includes harassment, intimidation, doxxing, deliberate disclosure of secrets or private data, deceptive evidence, plagiarism, spam, and repeated attempts to derail technical discussion after maintainers have set a boundary.

## Scope

This policy applies to repository issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions, release coordination, and other project spaces where a participant is representing the project.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may edit or remove contributions that violate this policy and may temporarily or permanently restrict participation when necessary to protect the project or its participants. Enforcement decisions should be proportionate, documented when appropriate, and based on behavior rather than disagreement.

For security-sensitive matters, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead of publishing sensitive details in a public issue.
